root_cause.text: The bounds check in the stm32-usphyc probe function uses `>` instead of `>=`, allowing an index equal to the array size to pass validation and subsequently access one element beyond the allocated usbphyc->phys[] array.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes line 715 from `if (ret || index > usbphyc->nphys)` to `if (ret || index >= usbphyc->nphys)`. Since the usbphyc->phys[] array has usbphyc->nphys elements (valid indices 0 to nphys-1), an index value equal to nphys is out of bounds. The original condition only rejected indices strictly greater than nphys, permitting index == nphys to proceed and cause an out-of-bounds array access.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix off-by-one error in array bounds validation by rejecting index values equal to nphys, not just those exceeding it.
intent_record.what: Changed the boundary check condition from `index > usbphyc->nphys` to `index >= usbphyc->nphys` on line 715.
intent_record.how: This change tightens the validation logic to reject index values that are equal to or greater than nphys, rather than only those strictly greater than nphys. Since array indexing is typically 0-based, an index equal to nphys would be out-of-bounds. This prevents potential buffer overflows or out-of-bounds memory access when the index is used to access an array of size nphys.

Since array indices are 0-based and nphys represents the array size, an index equal to nphys is out of bounds. bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 94c358da3a0545205c6c6a50ae26141f1c73acfa
Author: Amelie Delaunay <amelie.delaunay@st.com>
Date:   Fri Mar 2 15:56:25 2018 +0100

    phy: stm32: add support for STM32 USB PHY Controller (USBPHYC)
    
    This patch adds phy transceiver driver for STM32 USB PHY Controller
    (USBPHYC) that provides dual port High-Speed phy for OTG (single port)
    and EHCI/OHCI host controller (two ports).
    One port of the phy is shared between the two USB controllers through
    a UTMI+ switch.
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable bounds check is present in the stm32_usbphyc_probe function at line 381-382: 'ret = of_property_read_u32(child, "reg", &index); if (ret || index > usbphyc->nphys)'. This uses '>' instead of '>=', allowing an index equal to usbphyc->nphys to pass validation. Since usbphyc->phys is allocated with size usbphyc->nphys (line 365-367), an index equal to nphys would cause an out-of-bounds access when used at line 384: 'usbphyc->phys[port] = usbphyc_phy'. The vulnerability exists because the check should be 'index >= usbphyc->nphys' to properly reject indices at or beyond the array size.
